messages.author: f3e53d88c5f2bedb
messages.subject: Issues with measurementInvarianceCat
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to test a model for measurement invariance with a grouping variable with 2 levels, using ordinal 7-point Likert data.

model = "
f4 <~ i8
f4 =~ f1 + f2 + f3

f1 =~ i1 + i2 + i3
f2 =~ i4 + i5
f3 =~ i6 + i7
"

measurementInvariance(model, data, group="g", estimator="WLSMV")

I get the following error, with no further explanation:
Error in if (nvar < 3) { : argument is of length zero

I've tried just about everything I can think of to remedy the problem.

I've removed the formative indicator ("f4 <~ i8") from the model and the error changes to the following:
Error in if (numThresholdMarker[i] == 1) lavaanParTable <- fixParTable(lavaanParTable,  : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

I've then removed the hierarchical latent factor ("f4 =~ f1 + f2 + f3") so that all I am left with are the f1, f2, and f3 lines and get the following, even though it is a data frame with all ordinal factors and a factor for the grouping variable:
Error in lavData(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster, ov.names = ov.names,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: data object of class character

Does anyone have a clue of what may be going wrong? I can perform the analysis fine using the original model and measurementInvariance() with the variables as integers, but recognize this is the incorrect function to use given that the variables are actually ordinal and the theta parameterization should be used. Any assistance would be appreciated.

Thank you,
Richard

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Issues with measurementInvarianceCat
parts: I am trying to test a model for measurement invariance with a grouping variable with 2 levels, using ordinal 7-point Likert data.

I think you can safely treat these data as continuous:

http://psych.colorado.edu/~willcutt/pdfs/Rhemtulla_2012.pdf

Not that there is anything wrong with treating ordinal data as ordinal.  But unless you have a very large sample size, then estimating additional thresholds, as well as polychoric correlations in the face of even sparser bivariate contingency tables, could result in unstable estimation.
I've removed the formative indicator ("f4 <~ i8") from the model

I would do that anyway, since it's inclusion makes this a "full SEM" rather than only a measurement model (CFA).  

http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/15366367.2015.1016343

If you want to test invariance in the context of formative "measurement", you should not use these automated functions, but instead write the model syntax to fit the models you need to test whatever your hypotheses are.

I've then removed the hierarchical latent factor ("f4 =~ f1 + f2 + f3") so that all I am left with are the f1, f2, and f3 lines and get the following, even though it is a data frame with all ordinal factors and a factor for the grouping variable:
Error in lavData(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster, ov.names = ov.names,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: data object of class character

Does anyone have a clue of what may be going wrong? I can perform the analysis fine using the original model and measurementInvariance() with the variables as integers, but recognize this is the incorrect function to use given that the variables are actually ordinal and the theta parameterization should be used.

If you do want to continue treating the variables as ordinal, then the measurementInvarianceCat() function is the one you want to use.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Issues with measurementInvarianceCat
parts:
model = "
f4 =~ f1 + f2 + f3

f1 =~ i1 + i2 + i3
f2 =~ i4 + i5
f3 =~ i6 + i7
"

The measurementInvarianceCat() function only works for categorical indicators.  You have a second-order factor whose indicators are normally distributed latent constructs, not categorical items.  These automated function are only designed for simple cases, so you are better off specifying your models manually.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
